items.title: Mandelson tried to influence Starmer’s cabinet reshuffle, new documents reveal – UK politics live
items.desc: In a WhatsApp exchange Mandelson told Starmer’s chief of staff at the time, Morgan McSweeney, to ‘solve your Darren issue’ – referring to Darren Jones The Liberal Democrats are saying the UK needs a proper plan for immigration. This is from the party’s asylum and immigration spokesperson, Paul Kohler . Britain needs to regain control of its immigration system after the chaos of Brexit. Yet sixteen years after David Cameron’s ‘tens of thousands’ pledge, six prime ministers and ten home secretaries have overseen wild swings in immigration numbers with net migration now set to fall below zero. Britain faces serious demographic and economic challenges, and urgently needs a proper immigration plan to support our economy and public services. The fall in net migration is mainly a result of changes made by the previous Conservative government. We now need to go even further with a legally bindin

items.title: Double jeopardy killer recommended for release from prison
items.desc: William Dunlop, who strangled Julie Hogg in County Durham, was jailed after a double jeopardy law change.

items.title: UK bill to implement EU deal will allow ministers to enact closer ties in future
items.desc: Further deals can be enacted via same legislation, though it excludes rejoining single market, customs union or bloc as a whole A bill to implement the UK-EU deal will grant significant powers for ministers to enact even closer ties with Brussels, though it will stop short of Labour’s red lines. The government put what it is calling the “cutting costs bill” before parliament on Thursday, beginning the legislation to put the deal into law after it was agreed with the EU last Friday – though the deal to ease access for food and drink exports will not come into force until 2028, with the emissions trading deal to follow that year. Continue reading...

items.title: Labour’s split over Rosebank oilfield exposed by letter from nearly 100 MPs
items.desc: Exclusive: Frontbenchers join scores of party colleagues urging Burnham not to let ministers approve project Opinion: Why Labour MPs are opposing Rosebank Labour’s internal divisions over the giant Rosebank oilfield have spilled into the open, with nearly 100 Labour MPs – including a handful of frontbenchers – writing to the prime minister to express their opposition to the project. Ninety-two backbenchers and at least four frontbenchers have signed a letter to Andy Burnham urging him not to let his ministers approve the scheme for the biggest undeveloped field in UK waters. Continue reading...

items.title: Rosebank rebellion: are resignations next? – podcast
items.desc: Close to 100 Labour MPs have sent a letter to Andy Burnham calling for him to reject the Rosebank oilfield licence. Environmental campaigners say it will create massive greenhouse emissions and conflict with the UK’s climate goals. Supporters believe the project could bring investment and tax revenues. This is the first major internal party row under Andy Burnham, and potential resignations – including from the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh – are not off the table Tell us what you think of Guardian podcasts with our survey here Send questions for Pippa and Kiran to politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com Watch episodes of Politics Weekly on our YouTube channel here Continue reading...

items.title: Man found guilty of attempted murder of seven people on LNER train
items.desc: Jury still deliberating on seven other counts against Anthony Williams A 33-year-old man has been found guilty of seven counts of attempted murder after he stabbed 10 passengers at random on a London-bound train last year. Anthony Williams of Peterborough admitted stabbing 14 people over two days on 31 October and 1 November 2025, including 10 passengers on an LNER service from Doncaster to London. He denied 14 counts of attempted murder. Continue reading...

items.title: New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause
items.desc: Text of the treaties was published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

items.title: Man who drugged wife for rape by strangers in Stockport tells court of ‘guilt and shame’
items.desc: Woman watches her sobbing husband speak about ‘the pain I’ve caused’, as nine men accused of roles in her abuse A man who drugged and raped his wife, and invited other men into the family home to assault her, sobbed in court as he told a jury he felt “guilt and shame” over “the pain I’ve caused”. The man, who cannot be named to protect the anonymity of his victim, looked gaunt and red-faced as he gave evidence in a trial of nine other men who are alleged to have raped or sexually assaulted the woman, or encouraged the abuse online. Continue reading...

items.title: Mandelson tried to set up meeting between Trump adviser and lobbying firm he held shares in
items.desc: Then ambassador to US wanted to discuss alternatives to World Trade Organization in ‘under the radar’ meeting, documents reveal UK politics live – latest updates Peter Mandelson sought to organise an “under the radar” meeting between a member of his former lobbying firm, Global Counsel, and an economic adviser to Donald Trump, while he still held shares in the company, newly released documents reveal. Mandelson’s attempt to organise the meeting followed a Foreign Office proposal of a “light-touch way” to protect him “against perceptions of benefiting [Global Counsel] in some way while in public office”. Continue reading...

items.title: UK net migration at lowest level since 1997 as asylum claims also fall
items.desc: Net migration figures of 77,000 in the year to the end of June mark the lowest this century outside of the Covid pandemic.

items.title: Marlboro maker Altria considering takeover bid for Imperial Brands
items.desc: Shares in UK tobacco company jump by more than 14% on news US rival is looking into making offer Business live – latest updates Imperial Brands could become the next UK company to fall to a foreign takeover after its US rival Altria announced a possible bid for the tobacco firm. Altria, whose Philip Morris division makes Marlboro and Benson & Hedges cigarettes, told the City on Thursday that it was considering an offer. If made it was likely to be solely in cash, it said. Continue reading...

items.title: Millions of people to see average monthly mortgage payments rise by £100
items.desc: More people face higher mortgage repayments when they roll off a fixed deal than previously estimated.

items.title: Number of Neets in UK falls below a million as Burnham pushes to tackle crisis
items.desc: Latest figure of young people not in education, employment or training remains close to highest level in a decade Business live – latest updates UK politics live – latest updates The number of young people across the UK not in education, employment or training (Neet) has decreased but remains close to a million as Andy Burnham’s government pushes to tackle Britain’s youth jobs crisis. As ministers prepare to make sweeping changes in response to Alan Milburn’s landmark report on young people and work, the Office for National Statistics said the number of Neets fell by 22,000 in the three months to September, to 959,000. Continue reading...

items.title: Ministers have ‘failed to make the case’ for Heathrow third runway, MPs say
items.desc: Transport committee says policy papers show expanding airport would fall short of pledges on economy and climate Ministers have “failed to make the case” for a third runway at Heathrow , according to a damning report by MPs. The Commons transport committee said on Thursday that the detailed policy papers laid out by the government showed expansion of the London airport would fall short of pledges on the economy and climate. Continue reading...

items.title: Scotland's top medical chief resigns on mental health grounds
items.desc: Scotland's chief medical officer has resigned, stating he does not "currently enjoy the good mental health necessary to continue" in the position.

items.title: Simon Jack: Is Poundland's US owner to blame for its collapse?
items.desc: Poundland's management and MPs blame the retailer's owners, Gordon Brothers, but the US firm says without them the chain would have collapsed last year.

items.title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

items.title: Contraceptive pill usage in Great Britain fell drastically in last decade, research finds
items.desc: Survey published in Lancet reveals ‘hormonal hesitancy’ on the rise – with implants and injections also increasingly spurned The number of young women using hormonal contraception fell drastically in the past decade, with social media fuelling the “hormonal hesitancy” phenomenon. New findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), published in The Lancet, found that almost one in five women in Great Britain at risk of unintended pregnancy were not using effective contraception. Continue reading...

items.title: 'I'd lost the plot': Disgraced Huw Edwards speaks in 'important' new film
items.desc: Channel 4 has said its new documentary giving disgraced former newsreader Huw Edwards the chance to speak about his crimes was "an important film to make".

items.title: Ministry of Defence signs £8.7bn deal with Babcock to maintain submarines
items.desc: Wes Streeting says deal will ‘get our subs out of the docks and into the sea faster’ amid scrutiny of nuclear deterrent UK politics live – latest updates Business live – latest updates The Ministry of Defence has signed an £8.7bn contract with the defence company Babcock to maintain Britain’s submarine fleet amid scrutiny of the performance of the country’s nuclear deterrent. The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, said the five-year contract would “get our subs out of the docks and into the sea faster”. Continue reading...

items.title: Government's antisemitism adviser launches investigation into BBC
items.desc: Lord Mann says he has launched the investigation after "growing discomfort among Jewish BBC staff".

items.title: Faulty electrical goods returned to UK supermarkets ending up on Ghana ‘megadump’
items.desc: Mountains of household items are burned and stripped down at the tip by workers without protection such as masks, investigation alleges Electrical goods that were returned as faulty to leading British stores including Tesco, Argos and Asda have been found dumped on a waste tip in Ghana, an investigation has found. The faulty electrical appliances, including toasters and slow cookers, had been returned to major UK supermarkets. They were found at Agbogbloshie, one of the world’s largest e-waste sites, in Ghana’s capital, Accra, a joint investigation by Unearthed and Greenpeace Africa has found. The findings raise serious questions about e-waste export rules. Continue reading...

items.desc: Ethan Ives-Griffiths' father says concerns about his son's safety "weren't heard" before his murder.

items.title: Welsh first minister accuses Burnham of ‘casually’ rejecting devolution calls
items.desc: Rhun ap Iorwerth says PM is treating Wales with less respect than English regions and has ‘let himself down’ UK politics live – latest updates The Welsh first minister has launched a fierce attack on Andy Burnham, accusing him of “casually” rejecting calls to hand over more powers to the Welsh government. In an interview with the Guardian, Rhun ap Iorwerth said Burnham was treating Wales with less respect than he was showing to English regions, had little understanding of how devolution worked in Wales and had “let himself down”. Continue reading...

items.title: Michael Giles, co-founder and drummer of King Crimson, dies aged 84
items.desc: The British musician brought deft playing to prog masterpiece In the Court of the Crimson King, then worked as a session musician with the likes of Bryan Ferry Michael Giles, the drummer who co-founded prog rockers King Crimson, has died aged 84. The news was announced by King Crimson’s record label DGM, who said he died on Monday 23 November, but did not give a cause of death. Continue reading...

items.title: Dubai wholesaler plans renewed bid for collapsed Poundland
items.desc: The Dubai-based businessman who emerged as a suitor for Poundland days before its collapse into insolvency is planning a fresh bid to buy the retailer out of administration.

items.title: UK regulator admits error in calculating car finance compensation payments
items.desc: FCA also tells Barclays to stop making settlement offers while it works through data problems Business live – latest updates The financial regulator has admitted that it has miscalculated part of the compensation scheme for victims of the car finance scandal and told Barclays to stop making settlement offers while it works through the data problems. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) revealed it had identified “some errors in how we categorised a small group of loan agreements’, which will affect the average compensation payout to drivers. Continue reading...

items.title: Details of two treaties at heart of Andy Burnham’s EU reset to be published
items.desc: Government also to publish bill that will enact EU deals as Tories and Reform hit out over 10-year termination clause Europe live – latest updates Business live – latest updates Details of two treaties at the heart of Andy Burnham’s post- Brexit reset plans will be published on Thursday alongside the bill that will implement the changes into UK law. The treaties signed by the UK and the European Union at last week’s summit will have a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party were to end the agreement, they would have to pay to rebuild border checks infrastructure, the BBC reported on Thursday. Continue reading...

items.title: UK writes to veterans to ready them for possibility of mobilisation
items.desc: The UK has written to around 100,000 former military personnel to ready them for the possibility of mobilisation in the event of war.

items.title: UK net migration falls to lowest level in three decades, excluding pandemic
items.desc: UK net migration fell to 77,000 in the year to June 2026, provisional new data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) shows.

items.title: UK watchdog calls for shake-up of private dentistry market amid ‘catalogue of concerns’
items.desc: CMA report highlights inflation-busting annual rises and practices that ‘may not operate in patients’ best interests’ Tell us: what is your experience of UK private dentistry? Business live – latest updates The UK’s competition watchdog has called for a shake-up of the £8bn private dentistry market , after an investigation identified a “catalogue of concerns” including inflation-busting annual rises and evidence of targets to sell more expensive treatments and dental payment plans. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) said patients faced substantial differences in prices in different parts of the UK and “commercial practices, targets and incentives [that] may not operate in patients’ best interests”. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘It’s in quite a dark place’: why UK housebuilding is struggling
items.desc: The sector is in retreat across parts of the county, with developments paused. Despite a grim outlook for 2027 there is some cause for hope A shopping centre in London that was due to be knocked down and replaced with a retail emporium and more than 1,000 apartments has been paused , dealing another blow to the government’s housing targets. Lewisham council’s Green administration, which swept into power in May, insisted a larger number of affordable homes should be included in plans agreed last year with Labour officials. Continue reading...

items.title: London commuters braced for disruption as tube strike begins
items.desc: Industrial action by RMT drivers expected to cause severe disruption on Thursday and Friday Severe disruption is expected across the London Underground on Thursday and Friday, when many tube drivers will go on strike. Drivers who are part of the national union of rail, maritime and transport workers (RMT) will strike for 24 hours from noon on Thursday, in the first of a fresh wave of strikes in the long-running dispute over the planned introduction of a four-day working week. Continue reading...

items.title: Welfare overhaul plans put rare focus on improving benefits system for disabled claimants
items.desc: Timms review tackles some big questions about a flawed system – but leaves other issues in the ‘maybe later’ drawer Stephen Timms would be forgiven for feeling his thunder has been stolen. The minister for social security has spent the last year reviewing personal independence payments (Pip) in light of Keir Starmer’s doomed measures last summer, but last week the Milburn review pitched a set of changes to the key disability benefit to great fanfare. But when Timms took to the House of Commons to call for a “fundamental overhaul” of Pip on Tuesday, it was clear these were altogether bigger – and notably not explicitly cost-saving – ideas. Continue reading...

items.title: Patrick Radden Keefe’s London Falling named Waterstones book of the year
items.desc: The word-of-mouth success of the journalist’s investigation into the death of a London teenager is ‘one of the defining features of the literary year’ London Falling, Patrick Radden Keefe’s bestselling investigation into the mysterious death of a London teenager, has been named Waterstones book of the year. The book follows the parents of Zac Brettler, a 19-year-old who fell from the balcony of a luxury London apartment after pretending to be the son of a wealthy Russian oligarch, as they discover the murky, dangerous underworld of the city that their son had been drawn into. Continue reading...

items.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist in Duran Duran, dies aged 65
items.desc: Musician who had huge 1980s chart success had been diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2018 Duran Duran was transformed by Andy Taylor’s rock edge – and never quite the same without him Andy Taylor – a life in pictures Andy Taylor, the guitarist with 80s pop megastars Duran Duran, has died aged 65. He had been diagnosed with stage four metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, which he disclosed publicly in 2022 when Duran Duran were about to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Continue reading...

items.title: UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, Bank of England says
items.desc: Sharp rise expected as cost pressures mount, with experts factoring in energy price cap hike and potential impact of El Niño Food price inflation in the UK could hit 5% next year, the Bank of England has said, despite rising less sharply than feared since the onset of the Iran war. The deputy governor Clare Lombardelli told MPs on the cross-party Treasury select committee: “Food price inflation is coming in under what we expected [it] to be, and in fact under what the industry expected it to be.” Continue reading...

items.title: Treasury raises cost concerns over Milburn plan on youth unemployment
items.desc: Chancellor wants system laid out in Alan Milburn’s review to break even at an earlier date, sources say The Treasury has raised concerns about the level of spending on support proposed in Alan Milburn’s review into youth unemployment, amid pressure for the welfare bill to start reducing more quickly. Whitehall sources have told the Guardian that the chancellor, John Healey, is not happy with the level of spending required under the proposals and wants the system to break even at an earlier date. Continue reading...
